questions.problem:
What is the quotient of $15{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}-15x-11$ divided by $3{x}^{2}-x-4?$

The quotient is
{{field-1}}.
questions.worked_solution:
Using the method of polynomial division, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,\,\,\,5x+2 \\  & 3{x}^{2}-x-4\,\enclose{longdiv}{\,\,15{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}-15x-11\,\,} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,{15{x}^{3}-5{x}^{2}-20x}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,6{x}^{2}+5x-11 \\  & \,\,\,\,\,{6{x}^{2}-2x-8}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,7x-3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

- the quotient is $5x+2,$ and

- the remainder is $7x-3.$

questions.problem: What is the remainder when $3{x}^{3}-12{x}^{2}-87x-12$ is divided by ${x}^{2}-5x-24?$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the method of polynomial division, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,\,\,\,3x+3 \\  & {x}^{2}-5x-24\,\enclose{longdiv}{\,\,3{x}^{3}-12{x}^{2}-87x-12\,\,} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,{3{x}^{3}-15{x}^{2}-72x}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,3{x}^{2}-15x-12 \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,{3{x}^{2}-15x-72}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,60\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

- the quotient is $3x+3,$ and

- the remainder is $60.$

questions.problem: What is the remainder when  $27{x}^{3}+8$ is divided by $9{x}^{2}-6x+4?$
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that the dividend is missing the ${x}^{2}$ and $x$ terms. So, we first rewrite it by including the missing terms with zero coefficients, as follows:

$$
27{x}^{3}+8=27{x}^{3}+0{x}^{2}+0x+8
$$

Now, using the method of polynomial division, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,\,\,\,3x+2 \\  & 9{x}^{2}-6x+4\,\enclose{longdiv}{\,\,27{x}^{3}+0{x}^{2}+0x+8\,\,} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,{27{x}^{3}-18{x}^{2}+12x}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,18{x}^{2}-12x+8 \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,{18{x}^{2}-12x+8}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

- the quotient is $3x+2,$ and

- the remainder is $0.$

questions.problem: What is the quotient of $2{x}^{4}-{x}^{2}-1$ divided by $2{x}^{2}+1?$
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that the dividend is missing the ${x}^{3}$ and $x$ terms. So, we first rewrite it by including the missing terms with zero coefficients, as follows:

$$
2{x}^{4}-{x}^{2}-1=2{x}^{4}+0{x}^{3}-{x}^{2}+0x-1
$$

Now, using the method of polynomial division, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,\,\,\,{x}^{2}-1 \\  & 2{x}^{2}+1\,\enclose{longdiv}{\,\,2{x}^{4}+0{x}^{3}-{x}^{2}+0x-1\,\,} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,{2{x}^{4}+0{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,-\,2{x}^{2}+0x-1 \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,{-\,\,2{x}^{2}+0x-1}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, 

- the quotient is ${x}^{2}-1,$ and

- the remainder is $0.$

questions.problem: What is the remainder when ${x}^{4}+{x}^{2}+2$ is divided by ${x}^{2}+x+1?$
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that the dividend is missing the ${x}^{3}$ and $x$ terms. So, we first rewrite it by including the missing terms with zero coefficients, as follows:

$$
{x}^{4}+{x}^{2}+2={x}^{4}+0{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}+0x+2
$$

Now, using the method of polynomial division, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,\,\,\,{x}^{2}-x+1 \\  & {x}^{2}+x+1\,\enclose{longdiv}{\,\,{x}^{4}+0{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}+0x+2\,\,} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,{{x}^{4}+{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,-{x}^{3}+0{x}^{2}+0x+2 \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,{-\,{x}^{3}-{x}^{2}-x}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,{x}^{2}+x+2 \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,{{x}^{2}+x+1}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

- the quotient is ${x}^{2}-x+1,$ and

- the remainder is $1.$

questions.problem: What is the remainder when ${x}^{4}+2{x}^{3}-1$ is divided by ${x}^{2}+1?$
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that the dividend is missing the ${x}^{2}$ and $x$ terms. So, we first rewrite it by including the missing terms with a coefficient of zero, as follows:

$$
{x}^{4}+2{x}^{3}-1={x}^{4}+2{x}^{3}+0{x}^{2}+0x-1
$$

Now, using the method of polynomial division, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,\,{x}^{2}+2x-1 \\  & {x}^{2}+1\,\enclose{longdiv}{\,\,{x}^{4}+2{x}^{3}+0{x}^{2}+0x-1\,\,\,\,} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,{{x}^{4}+0{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,2{x}^{3}-{x}^{2}+0x-1 \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,{2{x}^{3}+0{x}^{2}+2x}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,-{x}^{2}-2x-1 \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{-{x}^{2}+0x-1}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,-2x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

- the quotient is ${x}^{2}+2x-1,$ and

- the remainder is $-2x.$

canonical_examples.problem: Determine the quotient and remainder of $6x^3-x^2+3x+1$ divided by $3x^2+x+2.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Using the method of polynomial division, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,\,\,\,2x-1 \\  & 3{x}^{2}+x+2\,\enclose{longdiv}{\,\,6{x}^{3}-{x}^{2}+3x+1\,\,} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,{6{x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}+4x}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,-3{x}^{2}-x+1 \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,{-\,3{x}^{2}-x-2}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

- the quotient is ${\color{blue}2x-1},$ and

- the remainder is ${\color{red}3}.$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Dividing Polynomials When the Dividend Contains Zero Coefficients
canonical_examples.problem:
Find the quotient and remainder of the following division problem:

$$
\dfrac{2x^4 - 7x^2 - x + 8}{x^2 - 1}
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Notice that the dividend is missing the $x^3$ term. So, we first rewrite it by including the missing term with a coefficient of zero, as follows:

$$
2x^4-7x^2-x+8 = 2x^4+{\color{red}0}x^3-7x^2-x+8
$$

Now, using the method of polynomial division, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,\,\,\,2{x}^{2}-5 \\  & {x}^{2}-1\,\enclose{longdiv}{\,\,2{x}^{4}+0{x}^{3}-7{x}^{2}-x+8\,\,} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,{2{x}^{4}+0{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,-5{x}^{2}-x+8 \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,{-\,5{x}^{2}+0x+5}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,-x+3\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, 

- the quotient is ${2x^2 - 5},$ and

- the remainder is ${-x+3}.$

Therefore,

$$
\dfrac{2x^4 - 7x^2 - x +8}{x^2 - 1} 
= 
2x^2-5 + \dfrac{-x+3}{x^2-1}.
$$

We can rewrite this result as follows:

$$
\dfrac{2x^4 - 7x^2 - x +8}{x^2 - 1} 
= 
2x^2-5 - \dfrac{x-3}{x^2-1}
$$
